exposure: fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) between 180 and 240 minutes of life
outcome: CPAP failure (intubation and surfactant administration within 72 hours of life)
cohort: Inborn preterm infants with gestational age 24+0/7-31+6/7 weeks, not intubated on admission to the neonatal intensive care unit, and managed with CPAP for respiratory distress syndrome.
finding: A fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO2) >= 0.23 between 180 and 240 minutes of life was the strongest factor associated with and highly predictive of CPAP failure in preterm infants.
mod_finding: Vaginal birth was associated with a lower likelihood of CPAP failure compared to non-vaginal births.
birth_weight: Not specified for the entire cohort, but lower birth weight was associated with CPAP failure.
